title: Inside the Silicon: Analog Bits N2P2 Test Chip
gist: This is a promotional SemiWiki piece on Analog Bits' TSMC N2P test chip and evaluation board, which carries 12 analog and mixed-signal IP designs. The article cites silicon results: about 33 mV dropout from an on-die LDO at 0.75 V and 1.5 A, programmable droop and glitch detectors, PLL jitter within PCIe Gen 3-7 limits, and PVT sensors that need no trimming. Its thesis is that advanced nodes alone do not guarantee SoC success; power delivery, clocking and on-die sensing do too.

themes.theme: On-die power regulation and disturbance detection

insights.claim: Analog Bits' on-die low-dropout regulator measured about 33 mV of dropout at 0.75 V output and 1.5 A load, with nearly constant output from 60 mA to 1.5 A.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Low dropout cuts voltage headroom and power loss, which matters for power-limited AI accelerators.
insights.quote: At an output of 0.75 volts and a load of 1.5 amps, the displayed silicon measurements indicate approximately 33 millivolts of dropout.

insights.claim: Rapid workload changes create uneven current demand across an SoC, and resistance and inductance in the power path disturb core voltage. At low operating voltages even small disturbances consume valuable timing margin.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: As voltages fall at advanced nodes, local power regulation becomes a necessary design element, which expands the market for such IP.
insights.quote: At low operating voltages, small disturbances can consume valuable timing margin.

insights.claim: Analog Bits' Droop Detector uses programmable thresholds to flag supply droops, for example below 0.75 V. Its Glitch Catcher flags brief dips below a threshold such as 0.685 V, so the system can hold a suspect result, retry an operation or recover. The article frames glitches as both a reliability and a security concern.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Voltage-glitch detection supports hardware security against fault injection, a growing requirement in AI and datacenter silicon.
insights.quote: A voltage glitch can affect a calculation or create a security concern, even when the event is too short to appear in slower monitoring.

themes.theme: Clocking and sensing for AI and chiplets

insights.claim: Analog Bits' PLL measurements show jitter below the limits for PCIe Generations 3 through 7. Core-powered PLL options avoid dedicated analog supply bumps, which simplifies integration.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: PCIe 7 readiness points to clocking IP for next-generation AI accelerators and chiplet interconnects.

insights.claim: Analog Bits' PVT sensors on N2P silicon show a smooth temperature response and strong voltage linearity. Temperature sensing without trimming can reduce production test effort, which matters as stacked dies make local conditions harder to observe.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Trim-free sensing lowers test cost, and on-die sensing grows in importance with 3D stacking and chiplets.
